title: Risotto alle Cozze
subtitle: Mussel risotto with white wine and parsley
excerpt: Arborio rice cooked in the liquid from steamed mussels, finished with fresh parsley. The mussels release a deeply savoury broth that becomes the whole flavour of the dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Risotto alle cozze is a Venetian and Neapolitan speciality. The technique of steaming the mussels first, then using their cooking liquid as the stock for the risotto, is fundamental, the briny, mineral broth from mussels is what makes the dish. This is distinct from adding frozen seafood to a generic stock.

content.text: Risotto alle cozze works because mussels, when they open under steam, release a briny liquid full of flavour. That liquid, strained to remove any sand, is combined with fish stock and used as the base for the risotto. The mussels go back in at the end, just warm, still in their shells for most of them. No cheese here: parmesan does not belong with shellfish.

Steam the mussels: heat a large pan over high heat. Add the mussels and 100 ml of the wine, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until the mussels open. Discard any that do not open. Strain the cooking liquid through a fine sieve and add to the hot fish stock. Remove most of the mussels from their shells, leaving a few in shells for serving.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a wide, heavy saucepan over medium heat. Cook the shallots for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and chilli and cook for 2 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes.

Pour in the remaining wine and stir until absorbed. Begin adding the mussel-fish stock one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to absorb before adding the next. This takes 18 to 20 minutes.

When the risotto is almost done, stir in the shelled mussels and half the parsley. Taste for salt and pepper. The risotto should flow; add a splash more stock if needed. Drizzle with the remaining olive oil and serve topped with the mussels in shells and the rest of the parsley.
